aloe vera.campus_location: UCEV Science & Humanities Block, Medicinal Herbal Bed
aloe vera.description: Thick, succulent perennial herb with fleshy rosette-forming lance-shaped leaves containing clear therapeutic gel. Highly drought-tolerant with serrated spine margins and seasonal yellow tubular flower spikes.
aloe vera.medicinal_uses: Natural cooling agent; accelerates skin burn and wound healing, relieves acid reflux, nourishes hair and scalp, and possesses potent anti-inflammatory and antiseptic qualities in Siddha and Ayurvedic medicine.
aloe vera.ecological_significance: Remarkable xerophytic ground cover that retains soil moisture in arid microclimates and releases nocturnal oxygen via Crassulacean Acid Metabolism (CAM).

alstonia scholaris.common_name: Scholar Tree / Devil's Tree / Ezhilai Paalai (ஏழிலைப்பாலை)
alstonia scholaris.campus_location: UCEV Central Avenue, Near Central Library
alstonia scholaris.description: Stately, tall evergreen canopy tree characterized by distinctive whorls of 7 leathery leaves along each node. Bears dense clusters of intensely fragrant greenish-white nocturnal blossoms in winter and long pendulous pods.
alstonia scholaris.medicinal_uses: Revered as 'Saptaparna' in Ayurveda; the bitter bark decoction is traditionally administered for chronic malaria, respiratory congestion, dysentery, and purifying blood.
alstonia scholaris.ecological_significance: Provides an expansive avenue shade canopy along library paths, buffers acoustic campus noise, and serves as an important seasonal nectar source for moths and pollinators.

areca palm.campus_location: UCEV Administrative Block Quadrangle & Dean's Office Entrance
areca palm.description: Clustered multi-stemmed ornamental palm displaying graceful arching golden-green feathered fronds atop ringed bamboo-like cane trunks. Creates a welcoming, serene tropical courtyard ambience.
areca palm.medicinal_uses: Known for mild astringent and digestive applications; celebrated as one of nature's top biological air purifiers that removes volatile organic toxins.
areca palm.ecological_significance: Certified by NASA clean air evaluations as an elite bio-humidifier, actively eliminating airborne formaldehyde, toluene, and benzene in enclosed academic spaces.

banana tree.campus_location: UCEV Hostel Backyard & Agricultural Demonstration Plot
banana tree.description: Giant perennial herbaceous plant featuring spirally arranged emerald paddle-shaped leaves up to 2 meters long, supported by a tightly packed fleshy pseudostem and large purple floral bracts.
banana tree.medicinal_uses: Stem juice is widely used in Tamil home remedies to dissolve renal stones and aid bladder health; flowers balance blood sugar levels; leaves contain protective polyphenol antioxidants.
banana tree.ecological_significance: Rapid biomass accumulator with exceptional groundwater retention; provides edible biodiversity and biodegradable zero-waste traditional dining leaves.

celtis australis.campus_location: UCEV North Campus Perimeter Road, Boundary Greenery
celtis australis.description: Hardy deciduous shade tree with smooth silver-grey bark, sharply serrated ovate leaves, and small sweet dark-purple drupes that ripen in late summer.
celtis australis.medicinal_uses: Bark and leaves have astringent and soothing properties; used traditionally to treat gastrointestinal distress, heavy bleeding, and soothe irritated mucus membranes.
celtis australis.ecological_significance: Highly tolerant of urban particulate pollution, acts as an effective perimeter windbreak along the Kakuppam highway, and provides staple sustenance for wild campus birds.

china doll plant.campus_location: UCEV Dean's Office Courtyard & Academic Porch
china doll plant.description: Compact evergreen ornamental shrub adorned with dense, glossy, bipinnate emerald foliage with delicate lacy leaflets. Cultivated for formal sheltered porticos.
china doll plant.medicinal_uses: Valued for restorative aesthetic biophilic presence, promoting academic concentration, reducing indoor stress, and refreshing veranda air.
china doll plant.ecological_significance: Improves micro-climatic humidity around academic verandas and provides dense green screening for administrative buildings.

coconut tree.campus_location: UCEV Sports Ground Perimeter & Canteen Walkway
coconut tree.description: Iconic tropical monocot palm reaching 20-30m in height with a ringed columnar trunk and a graceful crown of pinnate feather-like fronds. Yields hard-shelled drupes with nutritious water and copra.
coconut tree.medicinal_uses: Tender coconut water serves as a natural isotonic electrolyte beverage; virgin coconut oil possesses lauric acid which exhibits antimicrobial, antifungal, and cellular protective properties.
coconut tree.ecological_significance: Fibrous root network binds loose sandy soils to prevent erosion along athletic pavilions, while providing renewable eco-friendly fibers, leaves, and food.

foxtail palm.common_name: Foxtail Palm / Nari Vaal Panai (நரிவால் பனை)
foxtail palm.campus_location: UCEV Main Entrance Gate Boulevard (Kakuppam Approach)
foxtail palm.description: Striking architectural palm possessing a smooth, self-cleaning ringed grey trunk and dense, plumose fronds that form a distinctive brush resembling a fox's bushy tail.
foxtail palm.medicinal_uses: Grown predominantly for ornamental value and environmental moderation; seeds and fibrous fronds utilized in sustainable crafts.
foxtail palm.ecological_significance: Forms an imposing welcoming avenue boulevard that filters vehicular dust and carbon particulates along the main approach road to the college.

hibiscus.campus_location: UCEV Girls Hostel Courtyard & Chemistry/Biology Garden
hibiscus.description: Perennial flowering shrub with glossy dark-green serrated leaves and brilliant scarlet 5-petaled flowers with a dramatic elongated golden-dusted staminal column.
hibiscus.medicinal_uses: Legendary Siddha herb for conditioning hair, preventing early greying, strengthening hair roots, cooling internal heat, and brewing heart-healthy flavonoid tea.
hibiscus.ecological_significance: High-value nectar repository supporting native sunbirds, butterflies, and pollinating bees across the college gardens.

indian almond tree.campus_location: UCEV University Auditorium Walkway & Open-Air Amphitheatre
indian almond tree.description: Broad pagoda-style deciduous tree with prominent tiered horizontal branches and large leathery obovate leaves that turn striking crimson and copper before autumn shedding.
indian almond tree.medicinal_uses: Leaf extracts contain antibacterial tannins used to heal skin eruptions; internal kernels contain healthy monounsaturated fats that boost memory and vitality.
indian almond tree.ecological_significance: Forms a massive parasol shade canopy over open-air walkways, dramatically lowering ground radiant temperatures during hot midday hours.

indian mast tree.campus_location: UCEV Main Entrance Driveway & Campus Boundary Wall
indian mast tree.description: Tall, slender, columnar evergreen tree with pendulous downward-sweeping branches and narrow undulating shiny leaves with wavy borders.
indian mast tree.medicinal_uses: Bark decoction used in indigenous medicine as a febrifuge to lower fevers, alleviate inflammation, and stabilize blood pressure.
indian mast tree.ecological_significance: Highly effective natural acoustic barrier that absorbs roadside traffic noise and intercepts particulate dust along campus boundaries.

lxora plant.campus_location: UCEV Central Campus Circle Lawn & Flagpost Borders
lxora plant.description: Compact evergreen shrub producing dense, rounded corymbs composed of dozens of small brilliant red or scarlet star-like tubular florets throughout the year.
lxora plant.medicinal_uses: Flowers are used in Siddha treatments to alleviate dysentery, soothe skin ulcers, treat boils, and calm ophthalmic infections.
lxora plant.ecological_significance: Perennial floral nectar reservoir that enriches campus biodiversity by sustaining butterflies, moths, and humming insects continuously.

madagascar periwinkle.campus_location: UCEV Herbal Garden, Science & Humanities Plot
madagascar periwinkle.description: Evergreen herbaceous subshrub with glossy oval leaves and 5-lobed salverform flowers in vibrant pink, violet, or pure white with a yellow or rose eye. Flowers non-stop throughout the year.
madagascar periwinkle.medicinal_uses: Globally famous commercial source of vinca alkaloids (Vincristine and Vinblastine) utilized in oncology chemotherapy; leaves traditionally boiled to regulate diabetes.
madagascar periwinkle.ecological_significance: Hardy drought-tolerant survivor that thrives in poor soils, providing continuous herbal medicine specimens for engineering chemistry students.

mango tree(mangifera indica).campus_location: UCEV Canteen Lawn & Old Campus Orchard
mango tree(mangifera indica).description: Dense, broad-domed evergreen canopy tree with aromatic dark-green leathery leaves, sweet-scented floral panicles, and succulent drupes prized as the national fruit of India.
mango tree(mangifera indica).medicinal_uses: Leaves contain mangiferin with anti-diabetic and antioxidant attributes; bark and seed extracts act as potent astringents for digestive care.
mango tree(mangifera indica).ecological_significance: Exceptional carbon sink tree providing abundant cooling shade for students, soil stability, and food for wild campus squirrels and birds.

manila tamarind.campus_location: UCEV East Campus Perimeter Fence Line
manila tamarind.description: Thorny, resilient leguminous tree with bipinnate leaflets and uniquely curled, twisted pods encasing sweet, spongy pinkish-white edible arils with black seeds.
manila tamarind.medicinal_uses: Rich in immune-boosting Vitamin C, polyphenols, and dietary fiber; bark extract treats toothaches, gum inflammations, and intestinal worms.
manila tamarind.ecological_significance: Symbiotic root nodules fix atmospheric nitrogen to naturally fertilize nutrient-poor campus soil while acting as an impenetrable living fence.

neem.campus_location: UCEV Engineering Department Courtyards (CSE / ECE / MECH)
neem.description: Venerated evergreen shade tree with curved pinnate serrated leaves and sweet-scented small white starry blossoms. Celebrated as the ultimate sacred multi-purpose pharmacy.
neem.medicinal_uses: Contains azadirachtin with formidable antibacterial, antiviral, antifungal, and blood-purifying properties; treats acne, cleanses wounds, and cures skin ailments.
neem.ecological_significance: Acts as an organic insect repellent, releases generous oxygen, reduces ambient courtyard temperature by 3°C, and regenerates depleted soil.

pomegranate plant.campus_location: UCEV Horticulture Plot & Faculty Quarters Garden
pomegranate plant.description: Multi-stemmed shrub or small tree with glossy narrow leaves, flaming orange-red trumpet flowers, and thick-rinded ruby-red fruits filled with jewel-like arils.
pomegranate plant.medicinal_uses: Ranks among the highest antioxidant fruits on earth (punicalagins); improves hemoglobin count, lowers arterial plaque, and regulates blood pressure.
pomegranate plant.ecological_significance: Resilient, drought-tolerant fruiting specimen that sustains beneficial campus insects and provides live botanical cultivation demonstrations.

sago palm.description: Ancient prehistoric gymnosperm cycad surviving unchanged since the Jurassic era. Displays a rugged shaggy trunk capped with a rigid, symmetrical rosette of dark glossy needle-tipped fronds.
sago palm.medicinal_uses: Stem pith historically processed for edible sago starch; provides unique biophilic educational value on ancient non-flowering seed plants.
sago palm.ecological_significance: Exceptional living evolutionary artifact demonstrating ancient botanical defense adaptations, extreme drought tolerance, and architectural landscaping.

tulasi.campus_location: UCEV Herbal Sanctuary & Campus Temple Circle
tulasi.description: Aromatic revered medicinal perennial herb with pubescent purple-tinged square stems, serrated purplish leaves, and terminal spires of minute lilac flowers with an intense clove-like fragrance.
tulasi.medicinal_uses: Premier adaptogen in Siddha and Ayurveda containing eugenol; fortifies immunity, clears respiratory congestion, relieves stress, and neutralizes fever.
tulasi.ecological_significance: Emits natural phytoncides that sanitize surrounding atmospheric air and naturally repel mosquitoes and disease-carrying vectors across campus grounds.
